context: Sv48 implements a 48-bit virtual address space using a four-level page table that translates a 36-bit VPN into a 44-bit PPN, requires bits 63–48 of 64-bit effective addresses to match bit 47 to avoid page faults, and supports megapages, gigapages, and terapages with LEVELS equal to 4 and PTESIZE equal to 8.

(not provided) ### **12.5.1. Addressing and Memory Protection** Sv48 implementations support a 48-bit virtual address space, divided into pages. An Sv48 address is partitioned as shown in Figure 71. Instruction fetch addresses and load and store effective addresses, which are 64 bits, must have bits 63–48 all equal to bit 47, or else a page-fault exception will occur. Bits 63-54 and 9-0 have the same meaning as for Sv39. Any level of PTE may be a leaf PTE, so in addition to pages, Sv48 supports _megapages_ , _gigapages_ , and _terapages_ , each of which must be virtually and physically aligned to a boundary equal to its size. A page-fault exception is raised if the physical address is insufficiently aligned. The algorithm for virtual-to-physical address translation is the same as in Section 12.3.2, except LEVELS equals 4 and PTESIZE equals 8.
